home.heroText: Plan your retirement, project your savings, discover which home you can afford and analyze your bank activity. Everything stays in your browser, no accounts and no sharing your data.
home.previewQuestion: How can I manage my finances?
home.previewTitle: This is how your money looks in NestEgg
home.previewSubtitle: A sample of the results you can get: projections, calculations and analysis of your finances.

home.retirement.title: Plan when and how to retire
home.retirement.text: Calculate the age at which you can retire, how much pension you can expect and whether your savings are enough to keep your lifestyle. Adjust your contributions and see how each year of earlier or later retirement changes things.
home.retirement.b1: Estimate your pension under Spanish regulations.
home.retirement.b2: Simulate retiring earlier or later and its impact on your pension.
home.retirement.b3: Include residence and living expenses during retirement.
home.retirement.step1: Enter your age, income, life expectancy and savings.
home.retirement.step2: Adjust monthly contributions and expenses during retirement.
home.retirement.step3: Discover your estimated pension and the minimum retirement age.
home.savings.title: Project your wealth, mortgage and investments
home.savings.text: See how much you can accumulate year after year with your monthly contributions and check how buying a home fits in: mortgage payment, purchase taxes and family loan, all deducted from your initial savings.
home.savings.b1: Register your income, monthly savings and current investments.
home.savings.b2: Calculate the mortgage payment and the tax burden of the purchase.
home.savings.b3: Track the evolution of your projected wealth year by year in charts.
home.savings.step1: Enter your income, monthly savings and existing investments.
home.savings.step2: Optionally add a home purchase simulation: price, down payment, mortgage or family loan.
home.savings.step3: Review your projected wealth year by year and make data-driven decisions.
home.hogar.title: Find out which home you can afford
home.hogar.text: Starting from your income and savings, the calculator finds the maximum price you can pay for a home, the down payment required and a mortgage payment that keeps your effort under control.
home.hogar.b1: Get the maximum price based on income, savings and debt capacity.
home.hogar.b2: Break down the down payment, taxes and renovation and furniture costs.
home.hogar.b3: Adjust the rate, term, LTV and the effort you are willing to take on.
home.hogar.step1: Add your household income and savings.
home.hogar.step2: Adjust rate, term, LTV, effort and purchase costs.
home.hogar.step3: Get the maximum price and the down payment you need.
home.finanzas.title: Analyze your statements and your real savings capacity
home.finanzas.text: Import your transactions as CSV or Excel and discover, without exposing your data, how much you spend in each category, what your investments return and how much you really save each month.
home.finanzas.b1: Import statements from your banks and brokers in seconds.
home.finanzas.b2: Group expenses and income by category and review your cash flow.
home.finanzas.b3: Measure your portfolio performance and the interest and fees you pay.
home.finanzas.b4: Create several profiles, manage expense sharing when living together and calculate joint savings capacity.
home.finanzas.step1: Export a CSV or XLS statement from your bank.
home.finanzas.step2: Import it and classify expenses, income and investment transactions.
home.finanzas.step3: Analyze performance and your real savings capacity.
home.privacy.title: Your data stays private
home.privacy.text: NestEgg stores your data in your browser’s local storage: it stays on your device, is not sent to any server, and there are no accounts or third parties involved. Data is kept between sessions until you delete it. If you want to keep a copy or move it to another browser, download it with the backup button and restore it anywhere.

page.privacidad.title: Privacy policy
page.privacidad.subtitle: Last updated: September 23, 2026
page.privacidad.intro: NestEgg is designed to keep your finances private. This policy explains what data is processed, where it is stored and which external connections the app makes.
page.privacidad.s1Title: What data is stored in your browser
page.privacidad.s1Body: Every piece of data you enter (income, savings, imported bank statements, profiles, parameters and results) is stored exclusively in your browser's local storage on your own device. Nothing is sent to a NestEgg server: we don't create accounts, we don't use remote databases and no third party has access to your information.
page.privacidad.s2Title: What your data is used for
page.privacidad.s2Body: The data is used only to run calculations, make projections and visualize the analysis of your finances within the app.
page.privacidad.s3Body: You can erase everything by clearing the site's storage in your browser settings, or the aggregator part using the 'Delete all' button for each profile. You can also download a backup with the backup button and restore it in another browser or device.
page.privacidad.s4Body: The app does not use tracking or analytics cookies.
page.privacidad.s5Body: If this policy changes, the date at the top of the page will be updated. Continued use of the app after a change implies acceptance of the current policy.

page.terminos.subtitle: Last updated: September 23, 2026
page.terminos.intro: By using NestEgg you accept these terms. NestEgg is a free, personal finance calculation and analysis tool.
page.terminos.s1Body: NestEgg is a personal finance simulation and analysis app. Results are indicative estimates based on the data you enter and simplified formulas; they are not financial, tax or legal advice.
page.terminos.s2Body: You may use the app for personal purposes. You may not exploit it commercially, redistribute it, or use it for unlawful purposes.

page.guia.title: Usage guide
page.guia.subtitle: Everything you need to get the most out of NestEgg, step by step.
page.guia.savingsText: Project how your wealth grows year by year: a paid savings account, investments and, optionally, a home purchase with its financing. Any change recalculates on the spot.
page.guia.savingsStep1: Horizon: choose how many years you want to project (30 by default).
page.guia.savingsStep2: Starting wealth: split your total savings between the paid account and the investments you already have, and set the expected return of each.
page.guia.savingsStep3: Monthly contribution: enter how much you save each month and where you direct it (account or investment portfolio). You can define ranges with different splits each year.
page.guia.savingsStep4: Optionally, weigh how a home purchase would affect your current situation: price, estate-agent fees (percentage over the price), renovation and furniture, and its financing (a monthly mortgage payment with APR and term, or a family loan).
page.guia.savingsStep5: Review the results: total saved, account balance, investments and the year-by-year breakdown with estimated taxes. Compare what you put in versus the total invested on the chart.
page.guia.retirementText: Find out when you can retire: estimate your Social Security pension from your contribution years, compare the scenarios with and without a pension and check whether your savings last until your life expectancy.
page.guia.retirementStep1: Personal details: current age, life expectancy, annual gross salary and contribution years.
page.guia.retirementStep2: Starting wealth: split your total savings between the paid account and the investments you already have, and set the expected return of each.
page.guia.retirementStep3: Monthly contribution: enter how much you save each month and where you direct it (account or investment portfolio). You can define ranges with different splits each year that will shape the flow of your savings until the resulting minimum retirement age.
page.guia.retirementStep4: Optional, debts that continue: a mortgage or family loan you are still paying, with payment, APR and term, to know the age at which it runs out.
page.guia.retirementStep5: Retirement expenses: fixed expenses are calculated from your monthly net pay, subtracting your monthly savings contribution and debts (while they last). At residence age, these fixed expenses are replaced by the cost you set for that stage of life.
page.guia.homeText: Find out how much you can pay for a home based on your income and savings, what down payment you need and what limits your purchase — all in one calculation.
page.guia.homeStep1: Income: enter your household's annual gross salary, individually or jointly if you are buying together.
page.guia.homeStep2: Savings: set how much you have available to put towards the home purchase and, therefore, how much you keep as your safety cushion.
page.guia.homeStep3: Property: state whether it is new build, how much you keep aside for renovation and furniture, and whether any estate agent charges a commission.
page.guia.homeStep4: Financing: interest rate, term in years, maximum financing percentage (LTV) and the monthly effort, as a percentage of your income, you can take on.
page.guia.homeStep5: Results: maximum home price, taxes and fees, total down payment, maximum mortgage and monthly payment. You will see which constraint dominates: your income or your available capital.
page.guia.financesText: Import your bank statements (CSV or XLS), classify movements, analyze expenses by category, income, interest and your portfolio's performance.
page.guia.financesStep1: Export a CSV or Excel statement from your bank or broker and press 'Import' to upload it.
page.guia.financesStep2: Select the source bank; duplicates are discarded automatically and you can review how many movements were imported.
page.guia.financesStep3: Classify: assign the type (income or expense), the category and whether the expense is individual or shared; filter by bank, category or type, or search by concept.
page.guia.financesStep4: View your finance summary: capital, total profit and average savings capacity.
page.guia.financesStep5: Explore the tabs: portfolio, account, income, expenses and movements, and filter by different time periods.
page.guia.financesStep6: Update the market prices of the products in your portfolio and check their current and annualized returns.
page.guia.profilesText: Organize the household's finances in independent profiles: each person imports their statements into their own profile and you can split shared expenses and view your combined savings capacity.
page.guia.profilesStep1: Create one profile per person with a name and a color.
page.guia.profilesStep2: Switch profiles in the selector so each person imports their statements into their own.
page.guia.profilesStep3: In the aggregator, open the joint tab (visible with two or more profiles) to see aggregated income, expenses and savings.
page.guia.profilesStep4: When classifying expenses, mark the common ones as 'Joint' so they count towards cohabitation. You can mark whole categories as 'Joint' or specific expenses.
page.guia.profilesStep5: Check each member's monthly contribution and the effort it represents over their income.
page.guia.backupText: Your data lives only in your browser. Download a backup to keep it safe or move it to another device, and restore it whenever you need. You decide where it is stored.
page.guia.backupStep1: Open the backup tool from the floating button and press 'Download copy'.
page.guia.backupStep2: Choose 'Everything' (all profiles and data) or a specific profile; a dated JSON file is saved to your downloads.
page.guia.backupStep3: Store the JSON somewhere safe: another folder, a cloud drive or an external disk.
page.guia.backupStep4: To restore, press 'Restore copy', select the JSON file and choose the destination: 'Everything' replaces the current data and 'Single profile' restores into one of your profiles.
page.guia.backupStep5: If the file contains several profiles, you are asked which one to restore from; check before confirming so you don't overwrite data.
